ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Madam C. J. Walker Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing care for high blood pressure found at a workplace screening, morning headaches and protein in the urine at last year's executive physical, in a company founder who travels most weeks. Concerns: She wants to keep building her company and keep traveling to her agents, and does not want to be told to slow down; She is worried that her kidneys could fail and wants to know plainly what the numbers mean; She wants a plan that works on the road: medicines, readings, food and tests. [S]

tr.td: Losartan 50 mg oral tablet, one tablet each morning
One tablet each morning, at the same home time when traveling
Losartan 100 mg oral tablet, one tablet each morning
Empagliflozin 10 mg oral tablet, one tablet each morning; stop on days of vomiting, diarrhea or not eating, and before surgery
One tablet each morning, with sick-day rules
Atorvastatin 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily
Ondansetron 4 mg orally disintegrating tablet, one tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea, for up to two days
Every 8 hours as needed for nausea, up to two days
Amlodipine 5 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily

list.item: Elevated blood pressure at intake (166/102 mmHg, average of two readings), first found at a workplace screening; ambulatory monitoring to confirm: resolved, confirmed [S]

Albumin in the urine (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 286 mg/g) with eGFR 54 by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation; she recalls protein in the urine at an executive physical a year ago, and those records are requested; to be repeated and investigated: resolved, confirmed [S]

Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by 24-hour ambulatory monitoring (24-hour mean 149/94, daytime 154/98, night 140/88 without the normal nighttime fall), with left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and mild hypertensive retinopathy; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented high blood pressure: active, confirmed [S]

Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (eGFR 54 to 55 mL/min/1.73 m2 by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation; albumin-to-creatinine ratio 286 to 294 mg/g; present for more than three months), most likely hypertensive kidney disease; bland urine sediment and normal-sized kidneys on ultrasound; 5-year kidney failure risk 1.6%: active, confirmed [S]
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 174 mg/dL; 10-year ASCVD risk 7.9% by the Pooled Cohort Equations (intermediate): active, confirmed [S]
Viral gastroenteritis after a sales convention, with mild volume depletion and losartan and empagliflozin held under her sick-day rules; no acute kidney injury; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

list.item: Founder and chief executive of a hair-care and beauty company with a national network of independent sales agents, most of them Black women, whom she recruits and trains in person; travels most weeks to conventions, churches, schools and halls to teach and speak [S]
Gives to scholarships, schools, the YWCA and civil-rights organizations, and has gone to court against racial discrimination [S]

Lives in the city in a house she owns, and is having a larger house built outside it; one adult daughter. Grew up in rural Louisiana and Mississippi and worked for years as a laundress before her business [S]

Eats most meals on the road at banquets, receptions and restaurants; cooks on Sundays at home, the Louisiana dishes she grew up with; uses a salty seasoning blend and smoked meats for flavor; drinks a lot of coffee and too little water when traveling [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: a glass of wine at some events, under one drink a week. No drug use [S]
Sleeps five to six hours on travel nights and seven at home; walks when she can between meetings; health insurance through her company [S]
Asks to be addressed as Madam Walker, the title she chose for herself [S]

tr.td: Establishing care for high blood pressure found at a workplace screening, morning headaches and protein in the urine at last year's executive physical, in a company founder who travels most weeks
Two-week review of the 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure and the repeat kidney tests, with a kidney ultrasound and a nephrology consultation
Two-week check of potassium and creatinine after starting losartan and empagliflozin, home readings, and the echocardiogram
Eleven-week review: home readings on maximum losartan, urine albumin, kidney function after a recent gastroenteritis, lipids on atorvastatin
Six-month review: blood pressure at goal, urine albumin, kidney function, hemoglobin, mood, and the travel season ahead
Same-day sick visit for viral gastroenteritis with sick-day rules

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Nephrology consultation at the two-week visit for albuminuria and a reduced eGFR found at 49: the likely cause, whether more tests or a biopsy are needed, kidney-protective treatment, APOL1 testing, and monitoring that fits her travel

Confirm the diagnosis outside the office: 24-hour ambulatory monitoring on a day at home, and a validated upper-arm home monitor with a correctly sized cuff that travels with her, two readings morning and evening for seven days, travel days included; recheck in two weeks

Kidney evaluation: repeat urine albumin and creatinine at two weeks, compared with last year's results to establish chronicity; urinalysis; kidney ultrasound; calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone and 25-hydroxyvitamin D at baseline; every eGFR reported by the race-free CKD-EPI 2021 equation; no ibuprofen or naproxen

Heart and vascular risk: ECG at intake and an echocardiogram for the left ventricular hypertrophy it shows; a fundus examination; TSH and A1c at diagnosis; lipid panel and 10-year ASCVD risk by the Pooled Cohort Equations

Food: sodium under 2 g a day built on what she eats, not a new diet: a salt-free seasoning blend for the dishes she cooks on Sundays, smoked turkey in small amounts in place of salt pork, ordering strategies for banquets and restaurants, water instead of a third coffee on travel days; video sessions with a registered dietitian between trips; no potassium-based salt substitutes until her kidney tests and any new medicines are settled

Work and rest on her terms: she sets her schedule; the risks of uncontrolled blood pressure and kidney disease are stated plainly and any medicines are chosen to do the work, timed to her home clock across time zones, with a written sick-day card for her bag; a protected sleep window on travel nights and walking during layovers; video visits between trips and laboratory checks on her days at home
Mood and stress: PHQ-9 at intake and yearly
Vaccines: influenza today; pneumococcal, hepatitis B and Tdap needs reviewed at the preventive visit; influenza and COVID-19 each autumn
Gastroenteritis: oral rehydration, ondansetron as needed, losartan and empagliflozin held until she has eaten and drunk normally for 24 hours, then restarted; a metabolic panel within a week

As the nephrologist advised: losartan 50 mg, increased to 100 mg at two weeks if potassium and creatinine allow; empagliflozin 10 mg daily; sick-day rules for both; potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after each start or increase, accepting a creatinine rise of up to 30%; urine albumin at about three months, then every six months; blood pressure goal below 130/80, lower toward a systolic of 120 if well tolerated, with amlodipine as the next medicine
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily, chosen with her after reviewing her 10-year ASCVD risk of 7.9% with CKD as a risk enhancer; lipid panel and ALT at four to twelve weeks
Amlodipine 5 mg added for home readings above goal on losartan 100 mg; every laboratory check booked on a home day before her trips are scheduled, by her office, after two missed checks
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home within six months, lower toward a systolic of 120 if well tolerated
122/76 in the clinic; home average 123/77 on losartan 100 mg and amlodipine 5 mg
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio lower by at least 30% within six months
286 to 294 mg/g at baseline; 128 mg/g at six months, 56% lower
Kidney function stable, without a fall in eGFR of more than 30% after starting treatment
eGFR 54 to 55 at baseline; 50 to 51 on treatment, a dip of under 10%
Sodium under 2 g a day using foods she likes, at home and on the road
Salt-free seasoning at home and ordering strategies on the road; restaurant meals still the hardest part
LDL cholesterol lower by at least 30%
174 to 98 mg/dL on atorvastatin 20 mg, 44% lower
Care that fits her work: every check scheduled around her travel, by her choice
Laboratory checks booked before trips are planned after two missed checks; video visits between trips

list.item: Independent in all daily activities; works long days and travels most weeks; no limitation in walking or climbing stairs [S]
Alert, direct, organized and quick; asks for the numbers and the reasons; mood steady; PHQ-9 score 4 [S]
